_comment_mutate: src/lib takes .tsx as well as .ts. The four React context files there were never deliberately excluded; the .ts-only glob simply never reached them and had left ThemeContext.tsx unmeasured despite its test file. The three negated files are excluded for two different reasons, and the distinction matters. constants-generated.ts is excluded on parity, not cost: it is machine-written from api/pkg/constants and its correctness property is byte parity with that source, which the Go test api/scripts/generate-ts-constants_test.go asserts directly by driving the generator's own collectConstants and generateTSOutput over api/pkg/constants/constants.go, so a changed value, a renamed constant, an added or dropped constant, or a hand edit fails go test rather than mutation; mutation scoring would add nothing that parity test does not already force. techniques.ts and themes.ts are excluded on cost, not parity: re-measured at this writing they hold 3282 and 683 lines, and what remains after the query and derivation extractions is module-level data plus the module-load-time cell constructors and step merger that build it: 57 technique entries with 25 animated diagrams totalling 116 steps, 60 glossary terms, the SLUG, TITLE and TERM cross-reference constants, two theme shadow strings, PALETTES at 8 themes by 2 modes, VALID_THEMES at 8 entries and THEME_MIGRATION at 9. Everything in both files is evaluated once at import, so under perTest no mutant there is attributable to any test and Stryker re-runs the whole suite per mutant; the pre-split measurement found every non-static mutant returned Timeout, which the aggregate scores as caught, so admitting them whole would report clock-kills as assertion-kills. The residue is not unguarded. techniques.schema.test.ts runs the shipped TECHNIQUES and GLOSSARY arrays through techniqueSchema's validators and asserts 57 techniques, 9 subsection slugs, 66 flattened slug identifiers of which 65 are distinct (a subsection may reuse its parent's slug), duplicate-slug rejection across techniques and subsections, relatedTechniques resolving to a technique or a subsection slug, diagram cells bounded to rows and columns 0-8 with values and candidate digits 1-9, animation steps of at least two with non-empty descriptions and no cell object shared between steps across all 25 diagrams' 116 steps, and a 60-term glossary with non-empty definitions, case-insensitively unique terms, and every relatedTerms entry resolving to a glossary term or a technique title without self-reference or duplication. themes.schema.test.ts asserts PALETTES covers exactly the 8 VALID_THEMES members, all 16 theme/mode combinations derive the canonical 34 tokens with valid values through themeDerivation, every palette carries all 25 required fields non-empty, themeToCssVars emits 34 unique --prefixed variables, and all 9 THEME_MIGRATION targets are valid themes that no legacy key shadows, with a negative fixture per validator. The logic that left the two files (techniqueQueries.ts, glossaryQueries.ts and themeDerivation.ts, plus the techniqueSchema.ts and themeSchema.ts validators these tests drive) sits inside the mutate surface below with its own unit tests. No e2e coverage is claimed for the residue: the Playwright specs run outside Stryker's Vitest runner and kill no mutants there.
_comment_thresholds: high/low are display thresholds (the portal reads them for its ok/warn coloring); 'break' is deliberately absent. A break threshold here was a second, independent gate at 90 while the real floors live in api/mutation-floors.json (hooks 100, surface 97), which is the two-sources problem. The enforcing gate is each scope's aggregate job in nightly-mutation.yml, which reads its floor from that file, and every shard step already runs continue-on-error because the aggregate is the scope's gate. Do not reintroduce break without deleting the aggregate gates.
_comment_dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Bounds one thing only: the single initial test run Stryker performs before any mutant is tested. It is not the mutation phase's budget; each mutant's own run is bounded separately by timeoutMS (5000 ms) and timeoutFactor (1.5), both left at their defaults, and it is those per-mutant limits, not this ceiling, that produce the Timeout kills. The value is measured, not assumed: across all 77 shards of hosted run 34928015321 the slowest initial test run took 90 seconds (median 84), and the same suite (2895 tests at local head f442807) measured locally at 4 minutes 08 seconds, or 8 minutes 28 under heavy concurrent load, so 20 minutes is roughly 13x the worst hosted shard and still 2.4x the most contended local measurement: a genuinely hung initial run fails in a third of an hour instead of two. It is deliberately unequal to both containing job timeouts in nightly-mutation.yml (surface 120, hooks 90): when the ceiling and a job timeout shared a number, a cancellation could not say which limit had fired.
_comment_ignorePatterns: Report artifact directories, none of which the tests read. Local allure-results alone holds ~422k files: unignored, ProjectReader spends ~100s walking them and the sandbox copy exhausts a tmpfs. A CI checkout is clean, so this matters for local iteration and costs CI nothing.
